title: NYC Artists Open Their Doors
summary: Open studios and houses, plus reviews of Betty Parsons, Riddikuluz, and the L train burlesque.

title: “Cornell 7” Case Sparks Fury and Protests in Solidarity With Jane Doe
summary: A Nationwide Day of Action on October 8 gathered artists, activists, and survivors in a collective call for institutions to hold abusers accountable.

title: Art Films We Look Forward to Watching at DOC NYC
summary: Documentaries on a giant pencil that became a local watering hole, the afterlife of Frida Kahlo through her image, and collagist Romare Bearden are among the festival’s most enticing offerings.

title: Sara Flores Paints What the World Stands to Lose
summary: “Every opportunity to show my work is a platform to raise attention on the struggle for self-determination and cultural resistance of the Shipibo people,” the artist told Hyperallergic.

title: Roy Lichtenstein Has Lost His Luster
summary: He went from being a satirist of America’s ideals to a parody of himself, an artist content with other artists’ masterpieces.

title: Utah Groups Sue Trump Administration Over Nine Mile Canyon Construction Project
summary: The environmental organizations filed a suit against the Bureau of Land Management for approving the project that endangers centuries-old Indigenous petroglyphs.

title: Karachi Biennale Cancels Fifth Edition Over “War Conditions”
summary: The cancellation of the January 2027 event reportedly came without the input of the biennale’s curator, Noor Ahmed.

title: Jonathan Nez on Indigenous Perseverance
summary: The former Navajo Nation president running for Congress in Arizona speaks to Hyperallergic about his upbringing, how Diné culture shapes his political thinking, and the importance of historical memory.

title: Vermeer the Immortal
summary: Tracing the Dutch painter’s enduring influence, free back-to-school art supplies for NYC teachers, and a glitch at a Pioneer Works exhibition is unexpectedly illuminating.

title: The Trafficker Who Furnished the Museums of LA
summary: A team of researchers excavates the story of Earl Stendahl, a mid-century gallerist who shamelessly stole ancient Mesoamerican objects and marketed them to the institutional art world.

title: A Little Fantasy Goes a Long Way
summary: In this photography exhibition, works vacillate between intimacy and unknowability, like a fractured peep show.

title: NYC to Provide Free Art Supplies to Grantees
summary: Winners of the city's recently doubled grant for artists can also enjoy unlimited supplies from Materials for the Arts.

title: Finding Vermeer in Unexpected Places
summary: Artists, filmmakers, poets, and the art market itself still bear traces of the Dutch painter’s influence, writes historian Ruth Bernard Yeazell in “Vermeer’s Afterlives.”

title: When the Accessibility Conveyor Belt Jams
summary: A malfunction in Finnegan Shannon’s installation at Pioneer Works led to new insights.

title: A View From the Easel: Flor Khan
summary: “Here, I am allowed to play, to not know the answers, to let the message evolve on its own timing.”
